reference_findings.diagnosis: Potentially important coronary-origin anomaly; anatomical subtype and risk interpretation require specialist imaging review and correlation with symptoms.
reference_findings.risk_assessment: Variable / anatomy clarification; qualitative simulation label only, not a validated score.

investigation_reports.ecg: Resting ECG without acute ischemic changes; exercise-related tracing not supplied.
investigation_reports.laboratory_panel: Serial hs-cTn negative in the current resting assessment; CBC, electrolytes and renal function within fictional reference intervals.
investigation_reports.echocardiography: LVEF 60%; no resting wall-motion abnormality; coronary origin not fully visualized by transthoracic echo.
investigation_reports.coronary_or_other_imaging: Reference coronary CT angiography report: anomalous origin of a coronary artery from the opposite sinus with an interarterial course described in the fictional report. Exact vessel/course must be reviewed by specialist; invasive angiography alone may not fully define 3D course.
investigation_reports.initial_vitals: HR 68 bpm; BP 122/72 mmHg; RR 14/min; SpO2 99%; stable at rest.
investigation_reports.not_supplied: Any test not explicitly listed is not ordered/not available; it must not be interpreted as normal.

history.chief_complaint: Exertional chest discomfort and near-syncope during intense exercise.
history.history_of_present_illness: No known coronary disease. Symptoms during exertion require careful risk assessment; the case is not intended to reassure from age alone.
relevant_history: Family history and sudden-death history must be specifically asked

differential_diagnosis: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy or other structural disease

pathway_review.label: Obtain specialist congenital/coronary-anatomy review and correlate with symptoms
pathway_review.reason: The course and exact anatomy matter; do not generalize from “anomaly” alone.

pathway_review.label: Dismiss coronary cause because patient is young and resting ECG is normal
pathway_review.reason: Does not account for exertional near-syncope or anomalous anatomy.

pathway_review.label: Assume 2D angiography fully describes the 3D course
pathway_review.reason: Cross-sectional imaging may be needed to define the course.

reference_findings.safety_review: Escalation for exertional syncope/near-syncope, activity advice only by clinician, family history, imaging review, informed consent and specialist referral are tracked as educational actions.
reference_findings.simulated_clinical_course: Reference branch: specialist review is requested and case remains open pending anatomic risk characterization.
learning_objectives: Recognize that rare anatomy can be clinically important.
Use appropriate imaging to define course.
Avoid reassurance based solely on age or resting tests.
reference_findings.review_note: Synthetic scenario. Clinical values and pathway labels require qualified interventional cardiology review before deployment. Educational use only; not real-patient guidance.
